description: Deterministic, single-threaded discrete-event simulation on a virtual (logical) clock — no real sleeping or wall-clock timing. A single FIFO server processes requests one at a time; each variant differs only in when it 'sends' a request (immediately after the previous completes for closed loop, or at a schedule independent of server state for open-loop variants) and how it admits/records that send. This is what makes admitted/missed counts and response-time totals a deterministic recurrence rather than a timing-sensitive race.

PERIODIC_STALL.note: Every 50th request takes 10ms instead of 100ns — models a periodic GC-like pause.

GC_PAUSE_INJECTION.note: A single one-off 50ms pause at request 500 — models an isolated GC/stop-the-world event.

BOUNDED_OVERLOAD.note: Constant 150ns service time; paired with a 100ns arrival interval below, the server is persistently overloaded (arrival rate exceeds service rate).

correctnessInvariant: produced == admitted + missed for every (variant, dataset) pair. CLOSED_LOOP and OMISSION_CORRECTED_RECORDING never miss (missed == 0) because they only ever send after the previous request completes. CLOSED_LOOP's recorded response time equals service time exactly, every request — the literal 'hides queueing' property. OMISSION_CORRECTED_RECORDING's recordedSamples exceeds produced whenever a stall's response time exceeds the target interval.
